target.title: fix: duplicate assistant messages in Telegram conversation context injection [AI]
target.body:
<!-- This PR was authored by an AI agent. A human operator reviewed and approved the submission. -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users would see duplicate assistant messages injected into the conversation context block — the "recent history" text that OpenClaw embeds inside the last user message before sending it to the model. The duplicates waste prompt tokens and can confuse the model about what it already said.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation-context block merges assistant replies from two sources: the session transcript and the Telegram message cache. Both store the same reply, but with different timestamps (model response time vs. Telegram delivery time, typically 10–60s apart).

The dedup function (`resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey` at `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts:188`) included `timestamp_ms` in the key, so identical replies from the two sources never matched — the dedup silently failed for every message.

The fix has two parts:

1. **Drop timestamp for long bodies (≥20 chars):** Use a text-only dedup key (`text:<normalised body>`) so that the same reply stored in both sources matches regardless of timestamp. Short bodies keep the timestamp-qualified key to avoid false-positive dedup on common short messages like "ok" or "yes".

2. **Strip Markdown formatting:** The session and cache can store the same reply with different Markdown formatting (e.g. `**bold**` vs `bold`). Stripping `* _ \` ~` before comparison ensures formatting variants match.

The threshold (20 chars) matches the same pattern already used in the transcript-layer dedup. After the normalised body still meets the threshold, the text-only key is used; otherwise it falls back to the timestamp-qualified key (safe: no false matches).

## User Impact

Telegram users will no longer see duplicate assistant messages in the conversation context sent to the model. This reduces prompt token waste and improves model coherence.

## Evidence

**Before fix** — the conversation-context block emitted each assistant reply twice (once from session, once from cache) because timestamps differed:

```
#session:xxx  17:44:30  OpenClaw: Here is a sufficiently long reply...
#45xx         17:44:49  OpenClaw: Here is a sufficiently long reply...  ← duplicate
                             ^^^^^^^^ 19s gap = different timestamp_ms = different key
```

**After fix** — zero duplicates; each reply appears exactly once.

Unit tests in `bot-handlers.runtime.prompt-context-dedup.test.ts` cover:
- Timestamp mismatch (same text, different timestamps → same key)
- Markdown variant matching (`**bold**` vs `bold` vs `_italic_` vs `` `code` `` → same key)
- Short-body fallback (keeps timestamp in key, no false dedup)
- Edge cases (non-string body, missing/invalid timestamp, empty body)
